 Lifestyle Top Korean Cleansing Balms to Try in 2026
 Written By: BOSS Editorial
 Published: October 21, 2026 Reading Time: 8 minutes
 Share this story 
 A good first cleanse should lift makeup and sunscreen without leaving your skin feeling irritated. We compared six Korean cleansing balms and oils for this list, looking at fragrance and format.
 Top recommendation: Rael Miracle Clear Purifying Twist Up Cleansing Balm is fragrance-free and comes in a twist-up stick that needs no jar or spatula. The brand says it has been tested by a dermatologist and an ophthalmologist. In a brand-commissioned study of 40 participants, it removed 97% of long-wear foundation and waterproof mascara after one use. [1] 
 How We Picked
 Each balm was compared on format, fragrance status, price per milliliter, pack size, and eye-area safety guidance. The published specifications, ingredient lists, and brand-disclosed test results were reviewed as of September 2026.
 Format: The dispensing format determines how much mess is involved, whether fingers or a spatula touch the product, and whether it travels easily.
 Fragrance-Free: Fragrance and certain essential oils can be irritating for sensitive skin, so it’s helpful to know whether they’re included in a formula.
 Price per ml: Because a cleansing balm is used nightly, the cost per milliliter tells you what this habit costs over time [2] , not just at the register.
 Pack Size: Pack size determines how long one purchase lasts and whether it fits comfortably into a travel bag or only a bathroom shelf.
 Cleanliness & Hygiene: A balm you use every night should stay clean down to the last use. Jars mean scooping product out with your fingers or a spatula that has to be washed and stored; a twist-up stick dispenses it with no scooping and no separate tool.

 1. Rael Miracle Clear Purifying Twist Up Cleansing Balm 
 Best for breakout-prone skin: a fragrance-free first cleanse in an easy-to-use balm 
 The twist-up stick format is different from everything else here. You apply it to dry skin, work it in, then emulsify with water and rinse. A brand-commissioned clinical study of 40 participants found it cleared 97% of long-wear foundation and waterproof mascara after one use. It’s fragrance-free and has been tested by both a dermatologist and an ophthalmologist, which matters if you use it near your eyes every night.
 Format: Twist-up balm; no jar or spatula needed.
 Fragrance-Free: Fragrance-free.
 Price per ml: $0.38/ml, based on $18.99 for 50 ml.
 Pack Size: 50 ml (1.69 fl oz).
 Cleanliness & Hygiene: Twist-up stick dispenses the balm with no scooping and no separate tool to wash or store.
 What to consider: It comes in one 50 ml size, built to live in a bag as much as on a shelf.
 2. Beauty of Joseon Radiance Cleansing Balm
 This balm is built around rice bran oil, rice water, and a grain complex of oat and Job’s tears extracts [3] . Add water and it shifts from balm to oil to a milky rinse. It’s fragrance-free. The brand has disclosed third-party irritation testing, reported as non-irritating. At $19.00 for 100 ml, it’s $0.19/ml.
 Format: Jar with a spatula.
 Fragrance-Free: Fragrance-free.
 Price per ml: $0.19/ml, based on the $19.00 list price for 100 ml.
 Pack Size: 100 ml (3.38 fl oz).
 Cleanliness & Hygiene: Jar format means scooping with the included spatula, which needs to be washed and stored.
 What to consider: The jar-and-spatula format may feel less convenient.
 3. BANILA CO Clean It Zero Original Cleansing Balm
 A sherbet-texture balm built on olive and jojoba oils, with acerola and other fruit extracts [4] . Add water and it shifts from solid balm to cleansing oil to a milky rinse. Fragrance is listed as an ingredient. No clinical or third-party safety test has been published for it.
 Format: Jar with a spatula.
 Fragrance-Free: Not fragrance-free; fragrance is listed in the formula.
 Price per ml: $0.21/ml, based on $21.00 for 100 ml.
 Pack Size: 100 ml (3.38 fl oz).
 Cleanliness & Hygiene: Jar format means scooping with the included spatula, which needs to be washed and stored.
 What to consider: Consider another option if you prefer a fragrance-free formula.
 4. HEIMISH All Clean Balm
 A sherbet balm in a jar with a single-touch cap and spatula; add water and it shifts to a cleansing oil, then a milky rinse. At 120 ml for $18.00, it’s $0.15/ml. The formula contains more than ten essential oils, including orange peel, lavender, geranium, grapefruit, eucalyptus, tea tree, and bergamot, and the label lists limonene, citral, and linalool as fragrance allergens. No third-party clinical test has been published.
 Format: Jar with a spatula and a single-touch cap.
 Fragrance-Free: Not fragrance-free; the formula contains over ten essential oils and lists limonene, citral, and linalool as fragrance allergens.
 Price per ml: $0.15/ml, based on $18.00 for 120 ml.
 Pack Size: 120 ml (4.05 fl oz).
 Cleanliness & Hygiene: The single-touch cap helps keep the jar covered, but you still scoop with a spatula that needs to be washed and stored.
 What to consider: Consider another option if you prefer a formula without essential oils.
 5. Anua Heartleaf Pore Control Cleansing Oil
 This is a liquid cleansing oil rather than a solid balm. You apply it to dry hands, massage it onto your face, then rinse. The formula blends sunflower, macadamia, olive, jojoba, and grape seed oils with heartleaf extract. At 200 ml for $21.00, it’s $0.11/ml, though the amount used per cleanse differs, so the per-ml figure isn’t directly comparable to a solid balm. Fragrance is listed as an ingredient, and no clinical or safety test has been published.
 Format: Liquid oil in a bottle, applied to dry hands before massaging onto the face.
 Fragrance-Free: Not fragrance-free; fragrance is listed in the formula.
 Price per ml: $0.11/ml, based on $21.00 for 200 ml. As a liquid oil, this isn’t directly comparable to the per-ml cost of a solid balm.
 Pack Size: 200 ml (6.76 fl oz).
 Cleanliness & Hygiene: Bottle format means no scooping and no spatula; you dispense it onto dry hands.
 What to consider: This is a liquid oil, so it won’t give you the solid balm format the other picks offer.
 6. Then I Met You Living Cleansing Balm
 A sorbet-texture jar balm with a yellow tint from sea buckthorn oil, scented with rosewood, grapefruit, and rosemary essential oils. The retailer notes no synthetic fragrance in the formula. It’s sold by weight at 90 g for $39.00, which puts it at $0.43/g. Because it’s priced by weight rather than volume, that figure sits outside the ml-based pricing of the others. No clinical or third-party safety test has been published.
 Format: Jar with a spatula.
 Fragrance-Free: Not fragrance-free; scented with rosewood, grapefruit, and rosemary essential oils.
 Price per ml: $0.43/g, based on $39.00 for 90 g. Sold by weight, not volume, so this isn’t directly comparable to the ml prices of the other options.
 Pack Size: 90 g (3.17 fl oz).
 Cleanliness & Hygiene: Jar format means scooping with a spatula, which needs to be washed and stored.
 What to consider: Consider another option if you’re avoiding fragrance in your skincare routine.
 Bottom line
 Top pick: Rael Miracle Clear Purifying Twist Up Cleansing Balm, for a fragrance-free, ophthalmologist-tested first cleanse in a stick you can carry anywhere.
 Runner-up: Beauty of Joseon Radiance Cleansing Balm, a jar balm.
 Also great: Banila Co Clean It Zero Original Cleansing Balm, a jar balm; HEIMISH All Clean Balm, a jar balm; Anua Heartleaf Pore Control Cleansing Oil, a cleansing oil; Then I Met You Living Cleansing Balm, a jar balm.
 Frequently Asked Questions
 How do you use a Korean cleansing balm properly?
 Apply a small amount to dry skin, massage in circular motions to dissolve makeup and sunscreen, then emulsify with a little warm water before rinsing. Follow with a water-based cleanser as a second step, which is the standard double-cleanse method common to Korean skincare routines.
 Can Korean cleansing balms remove waterproof makeup?
 Most oil-based cleansing balms break down waterproof formulas reasonably well because oil dissolves the wax and silicone binders that make makeup water-resistant. Follow the product’s directions when removing eye and lip makeup, as application methods and recommended contact times may vary.
 Are Korean cleansing balms good for acne-prone or sensitive skin?
 Fragrance-free, non-comedogenic balms tend to sit better on acne-prone or reactive skin, while balms with added fragrance or heavy waxes can trigger breakouts or irritation in some people. If you have a known skin condition, a dermatologist is the right person to confirm whether any product ingredient list is appropriate for your skin.
